# TF_LABEL_CENSUS -- the Terraform-label census (LGIC_ENFORCE EN-t-1)

**Cell:** LGIC_ENFORCE `EN-t-1` (PRD candidate E8, its first half), task order `LGIC_ENFORCE.TO-EN-t-1`, written by
`0.9.0_WK_LGIC_ENFORCE~3` on branch `wk-lgic-enforce-1-3` off CLOUD @`fd9c9ca174`. Every file and line below is read at that
base, and every count is recomputable from the fenced json at the end.

## 1. What was graded, and with what

- **The instrument.** `lib/opal_naming.py` is absent at the base, so EN-b-1's `grade()` could not be called. This census
  applies `org/missions/D14/LGIC/LGIC_NAMING/deliverables/GRADING_RULE.md` **by its written steps** -- G1, G2, G3, then the
  grammar of the type (R, S, L, B, K), then G6; the first step that returns an output decides -- hand-coded in
  `deliverables/0.9.0_WK_LGIC_ENFORCE~3/instrument/census.py`, over a stdlib Terraform block scanner (`instrument/tfscan.py`).
  `writer.py` beside them writes this file.
- **The control on the hand-coding.** `python <instrument>/census.py selftest` grades the rule's own worked cases:
  **38 of 38 graded cases agree, 0 disagree.** 5 of the 43 cases are not graded by it: the platinum and tier-first key
  forms (K4a, K5, K6), which walk the LIST and are not hand-coded. **No Terraform name in this census needed them: 0 of 1332.**
- **The rule's vintage.** GRADING_RULE.md says it reads NAMING_SCHEMA.json v1.4; the base carries v1.6. The census applies
  the rule as written and reads the schema only for `kind.by_type`, `types_not_graded_by_kind` and `bucket.standing_shared`.
  Two later schema rulings the rule does not carry would move a grade here. `aws_fixed` (AW1, v1.5) puts log groups
  prefixed `aws-waf-logs-` OUTSIDE the domain, where the rule's G2.3 RAISES them: 2 name(s) here, `"aws-waf-logs-${var.name}"` (infra/aws/terraform/opal-gateway/waf.tf:22), `aws-waf-logs-opal-cloudfront` (infra/aws/terraform/portal-auth/waf-cloudfront.tf:282).
  And FN1 (v1.5) writes an agent noun as its verb (publisher -> publish), which no canonical form here applies. Row `LGIC_ENFORCE-W3-S4`.
- **Labels are graded, and kept apart.** A label is graded as a name of the node type its resource maps to (the order: *"grade
  them by the rule anyway, and keep them apart"*). NAMING_SCHEMA.json v1.6 lists "Terraform resource labels and module names"
  under `not_covered`, so every label verdict is the rule applied outside the schema's domain, on the order's word. Labels are
  snake_case by Terraform convention, so a label almost never equals its kebab canonical form; the label verdicts measure that,
  and the systems and scopes labels carry.

## 2. The denominators

- `tf_files` = **468**: `git ls-files infra/aws/terraform` restricted to `.tf`, at the base.
- `labels` = **2035**: every `resource "<type>" "<label>"` block the scanner reads, over 104 Terraform resource types.
  A raw line regex over the same files finds 2039 heads. The 4 it finds and the scanner does not sit inside `/* ... */`
  pre-stage comment blocks, so they are not Terraform and are not in the census: infra/aws/terraform/imo-pipeline/phase3-serving-consolidate-lambda.tf:91 `aws_lambda_permission.events_invoke_serving_consolidate`; infra/aws/terraform/imo-pipeline/phase3-serving-trio-lambdas.tf:116 `aws_lambda_permission.events_invoke_serving_companies`; infra/aws/terraform/imo-pipeline/phase3-serving-trio-lambdas.tf:157 `aws_lambda_permission.events_invoke_serving_employees`; infra/aws/terraform/imo-pipeline/phase3-serving-trio-lambdas.tf:201 `aws_lambda_permission.events_invoke_serving_scoring`.
- `name_attributes` = **1332**: one row per own-name attribute of a resource block (section 3).
- Top-level blocks that are not resources are outside the order's census: 9 `check`, 197 `data`, 119 `locals`, 146 `module`, 298 `output`, 75 `provider`, 74 `terraform`, 98 `variable`.
  The 146 `module` calls pass names INTO modules: 122 literal name-like argument(s) (122 `function_name`). They are arguments, not resource
  attributes, so they are not rows here; the module's own resource names them by `var.<x>`, which does not resolve inside the
  module (row `LGIC_ENFORCE-W3-S3`, which also records that the order's `role_name` is on no tracked resource block).

**The partition of the 2035 resource blocks.** Every block falls in exactly one line; the name rows sum to the denominator.

| class | Terraform types | blocks | name rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| maps to a graded node type, named by its own attribute | 28 | 1259 | 1259 |
| maps to a NOT GRADED node type (G1.2) | 6 | 86 | 7 |
| carries its own name, maps to no node type (G1.1 RAISE) | 30 | 66 | 66 |
| names nothing (attachments, targets, permissions, configurations, integrations) | 40 | 624 | 0 |
| **total** | **104** | **2035** | **1332** |

## 4. How a value is read

- **Literal** (`value_claim` = measured): graded as written -- 1208 of 1332.
- **Expression resolved in the same directory** (`value_claim` = inferred): `local.<x>`, a `var.<x>` default, or
  `aws_<type>.<label>.<id|name|own attribute>` of a same-directory resource, substituted into a template; `resolved` carries the
  string graded -- 100 of 1332. A variable default can be overridden at apply; no `.tfvars` file is tracked under
  `infra/aws/terraform` at the base.
- **Expression not resolvable** (`value_claim` = absent): `each.*`, a module input with no default, an index, or an
  attribute that is not a name -- 24 of 1332. A graded type's row RAISES at G3 (the tokeniser cannot place it): 22; the rest are
  decided at G1 before the name is read. Row `LGIC_ENFORCE-W3-S2`.

**Where the RAISES come from** (the step that raised):

- labels: G1.1 690, R1.f 467, G2.3 68, R1.c 60, R1.d 2, K1 2.
- name attributes: R1.f 181, R1.c 121, G1.1 66, R2 39, G3 22, B2 6, R1.d 2, G2.3 2, L4/L2 1, L2 1, K1 1.
- R1.c and R2 are a V2 token in the system slot (row `LGIC_NAMING-W1-S2`: `agentbus`, `globgrph`, `opsec`, `imo` and the
  rest wait on the registry's platform-subsystem rows). R1.f is a first token in no vocabulary. G2.3 on a label is a label
  graded as a log group, which never begins `/`.

**ALIAS:** 24 name attributes, 22 of them through the refused `bd` (R3: `bd` beside a firm is the vendor `blackdiamond`, alone
it is the firm `49financial`); the rest are a short firm form in a data bucket, which takes the long form (B2).

## 6. What this census does not decide

- Whether labels SHOULD be graded: the schema keeps them `not_covered` until their flagger is specified (E8, second half).
- The names module calls pass in (section 2), `data` sources, tag keys and values other than `aws_instance`'s `Name`.
- The Terraform-type map and the value resolution are readings (rows W3-S1, W3-S2), not rulings.
- FN1-FN4 and the other v1.5/v1.6 slot rulings the rule does not carry (row W3-S4). The K4a/K5/K6 LIST walk (0 names needed it).
- Nothing live was read and no Terraform ran: the values are the repo's, at the base.

## 7. Rows filed on the channel

`org/missions/D14/LGIC/LGIC_ENFORCE/surprise-channel/investigations/INVESTIGATION_v1.md`:

- `LGIC_ENFORCE-W3-S1` -- G1.1 grades a node type; Terraform types are not node types and the order gives no map.
- `LGIC_ENFORCE-W3-S2` -- 124 of 1332 name values are Terraform expressions, not names; 100 resolved statically, 24 not.
- `LGIC_ENFORCE-W3-S3` -- the order's `role_name` is on no tracked resource block; module-call names are outside a resource census.
- `LGIC_ENFORCE-W3-S4` -- GRADING_RULE.md is v1.4-vintage against NAMING_SCHEMA v1.6: G2.3 RAISES what `aws_fixed` excludes (2 names).

## 8. The rows

`labels` and `name_attributes` are separate lists. Beyond the order's fields each row carries `node_type` (section 3's map;
`null` = no node type) and `why` (the rule steps applied, in the worked cases' style). A name row also carries `value_claim`,
and `resolved` when the value is an expression resolved in its directory. `canonical` is empty on RAISE and NOT-GRADED.
